headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: Nullclaw’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can ingest and act on Airbyte outputs without a documented verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Nullclaw can read files, use MCP, run browsers, and process workspace content, so Airbyte outputs could be fed into it through shared files or APIs. Airbyte exposes an API and broad network egress, but no direct shared channel is documented. The pathway exists, but the exact bridge is inferred from profiles, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Airbyte outputs are written into a Nullclaw-readable workspace or MCP channel
IF Nullclaw treats retrieved content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable shared workspace mounts
Route Airbyte outputs through a schema validator
Block MCP access to untrusted content
Add a prompt-injection filter before Nullclaw ingestion
requires-engineering: isolate the agents with separate storage and no shared channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; Nullclaw reads and writes workspace files, handles secrets, and also has broad egress. If Airbyte data lands in Nullclaw’s workspace or API context, Nullclaw can exfiltrate it. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default-like setups, and the blast radius includes sensitive business data and secrets.
conditions: IF Airbyte exports business data into files or API payloads accessible to Nullclaw
IF Nullclaw is allowed to transmit its context or workspace contents over the network
mitigations: Keep Airbyte and Nullclaw on separate hosts
Remove Nullclaw access to Airbyte export directories
Disable outbound network for Nullclaw during ingestion
Redact secrets before any handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and Nullclaw can write files, modify git state, and use browsers/subprocesses. They do not share an explicit lock or coordination primitive, so concurrent writes to shared resources are plausible if both touch the same workspace or repo. This is a real conflict pathway, but not enough evidence for high because shared mutable targets are not explicitly documented.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or git repository
IF Airbyte-triggered automation and Nullclaw edits occur without external locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use a lock file around shared repos
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Nullclaw can act on browser, shell, git, and network tools, so if it consumes Airbyte-produced outputs as authoritative, it can turn upstream mistakes into downstream actions. Airbyte is a data pipeline/integration system, making it a plausible source of facts that Nullclaw renders or operationalizes. Because no verification boundary is documented, the cascade risk is high.
conditions: IF Nullclaw uses Airbyte outputs as facts without independent validation
IF those outputs drive emails, commits, web actions, or other side effects
mitigations: Insert a human review step before actions
Require source citations on all Airbyte-derived claims
Limit Nullclaw to read-only mode for Airbyte outputs
Log provenance for every downstream action
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source systems

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, while Nullclaw handles workspace files, audit logs, and multiple secret classes. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot prove a breach, but the combination creates a plausible retention and handling mismatch if the same regulated data flows through both. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF their retention or logging policies differ for that data class
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable logging of sensitive payloads in Nullclaw
Keep regulated datasets out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both systems
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
